# My plan for this year

Alright, let me think this through. I've been farming here in Quzhou for 20 years now, and with 600 mu to manage, I can't do everything by hand like my father did. I've got me, my wife, and my son who's mostly in school, so for a farm this size I hire workers — especially at wheat harvest, cotton picking, and stevia season. I own a tractor and a maize planter, and I hire a combine for the wheat.

## How I'm splitting the land

I'm keeping the same rotation I had last year because it worked out fine:

- **Wheat-maize double cropping: 400 mu** — this is my main business. The soil on those fields is good and the irrigation wells there are reliable.
- **Cotton: 150 mu** — these fields are on the western side, sandier soil, not as good for wheat. Cotton does better there and the price has been okay lately.
- **Stevia: 50 mu** — I started this a few years ago with the company contract. Takes more work but the price per mu is much better than grain. I'm not expanding it more because it needs too much labor at harvest and good workers are getting hard to find.

## Wheat (400 mu)

I planted the wheat back in early October last year — Jimai 22, same variety most folks around here use. It's been a decent winter, not too dry. Now in spring I need to top-dress and irrigate.

For fertilizer I put down about 50 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu before planting in fall — that's my base. Now at jointing I'll topdress 15 kg of urea per mu. So total nitrogen comes out to around 15 kg N per mu for the year. The extension guy told me years back that 18 kg N/mu is "right" for our yield level, but I think my base + topdress is enough, and fertilizer isn't cheap. If the crop looks yellow in April I might add a little more.

Irrigation: I plan 3 times — one at jointing (now), one at heading, one at grain filling. Sometimes I skip the grain-filling one if it rains enough in May. Pumping costs add up; each irrigation is maybe 30-40 yuan per mu with the meter.

I'm hoping for around 480 kg/mu. Last year I got 460. Wheat price has been decent.

## Maize (400 mu, after wheat)

Right after wheat combine leaves the field in mid-June, I direct-drill maize — no tillage, just straight in. The turnaround is 3-4 days, can't be longer. I use Zhengdan 958 or similar hybrid, whatever the seed dealer has that year.

Fertilizer: I band about 40 kg of compound fertilizer at planting, then topdress urea (about 20 kg/mu) at the big bell stage. Total N around 16 kg/mu. Maize is hungrier than wheat but the stalks from last year's maize and the wheat straw return to the soil help.

Irrigation: usually once or twice depending on July-August rain. If the rains come, I don't pump.

Pesticide: I spray for fall armyworm now — everyone does, the pest came a few years back and you can't skip it anymore. And a pre-emerge herbicide after planting.

Target: 520 kg/mu. The new hybrids are good.

## Cotton (150 mu)

I plant cotton in late April, after soil warms up. I use mulch film — saves water, warms the soil, and keeps weeds down. I buy fresh seed every year, can't save cotton seed.

Fertilizer: about 50 kg compound at planting, plus urea topdress twice during squaring and flowering. Total around 13 kg N/mu. Cotton doesn't need as much N as maize — too much N and you get vegetative growth but not bolls.

Irrigation: twice usually, at budding and flowering. Cotton is pretty drought-tolerant but irrigation at the right time really helps boll set.

Pesticide: this is where cotton eats money. I spray for bollworm, aphids, spider mites — usually 5-6 sprays through the season. No way around it.

Picking is the expensive part — I hire 15-20 workers for 3-4 weeks in September-October. Costs me more than the fertilizer and pesticides combined.

Yield goal: 260 kg/mu lint. Cotton price was 7 yuan/kg last year, not great but not terrible.

## Stevia (50 mu)

This is under contract with the company. They tell me what variety, give guidance on fertilizer, and buy the leaf. I apply about 12 kg N/mu plus compound, irrigate 2-3 times. Main cost is labor at cutting — needs hand work. The contract price makes it worthwhile but only on a small area.

## Total picture

Input costs I'm budgeting around 500-550 yuan/mu averaged across the farm. For 600 mu that's about 320,000 yuan out of pocket before I see any income. I've got working capital from last year's harvest and the cotton I sold in winter.
